output.reason: This lens compares NL-authored transition endpoints, initial-entry, retention, and disjointness contracts against the exact FCSTM closed-model topology (11 states, 33 transitions) plus the exact source inventory. Most NL transition endpoints are satisfied through the compiler's macro-generated route-token relay pattern (each authored source-target edge is realized via a routed pair: an outgoing segment setting R45RouteToken to a code, an ascend-to-owner completion transition consuming that code with matching guard, and a re-entry/decision at the owning scope). Root-level DoorShut/DoorOpen endpoints are direct. The DoorOpenWithItem group's alternatives are fully guard-disjoint (each token code is unique: 6/10/14/17/18/19 etc.), so the guard_disjointness contract is satisfied for the routed set. The NL4 alternatives specifically route through distinct completion codes (10 and then 11) which are disjoint. The two action/effect contracts (NL5-ACTION, NL7-ACTION, NL8-STATEACTION, NL6-EFFECT, NL8-EFFECT, NL1-DERIVED trigger, NL5-DERIVED effect) require action/effect content that pyfcstm's parsed guard/effect model expresses only as the R45RouteToken assignment, not as domain actions like 'display cooking time' or 'start timer' or 'stop timer' -- these remain unsupported semantic gaps (W1, predicate null) since no state entry/exit action or transition effect carries the domain-specific content; only the generic route variable is set. I flag these as candidates since the exact carrier transitions/states exist but lack the required domain content.

result.reason: This lens compares NL-authored transition endpoints, initial-entry, retention, and disjointness contracts against the exact FCSTM closed-model topology (11 states, 33 transitions) plus the exact source inventory. Root-level DoorShut/DoorOpen endpoints are direct. The DoorOpenWithItem group's alternatives are fully guard-disjoint (each token code is unique: 6/10/14/17/18/19 etc.), so the guard_disjointness contract is satisfied for the routed set. The NL4 alternatives specifically route through distinct completion codes (10 and then 11) which are disjoint. The two action/effect contracts (NL5-ACTION, NL7-ACTION, NL8-STATEACTION, NL6-EFFECT, NL8-EFFECT, NL1-DERIVED trigger, NL5-DERIVED effect) require action/effect content that pyfcstm's parsed guard/effect model expresses only as the R45RouteToken assignment, not as domain actions like 'display cooking time' or 'start timer' or 'stop timer' -- these remain unsupported semantic gaps (W1, predicate null) since no state entry/exit action or transition effect carries the domain-specific content; only the generic route variable is set. I flag these as candidates since the exact carrier transitions/states exist but lack the required domain content.

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, stable termination, cross-wrapper reachability, and dead-end frontier facts, using the closed FCSTM inspection-equivalent, verify, and SMT facts against the NL contracts. Key finding: the microwave PlantUML has a top-level DoorShut/DoorOpen/DoorOpenWithItem layer while the FCSTM instead nests all DoorOpenWithItem-scope activity under a compiler-owned wrapper reached through internal pseudo-exit routing (R45RouteToken) rather than direct named-state transitions. All NL-named states are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection-equivalent facts, and all declared events have reachable consumers per event_consumers facts, so root reachability and event-consumer coverage contracts are broadly satisfied at the structural level. However, several transition_endpoints contracts require inspection of the exact carrier because the closed FCSTM realizes each named-source-to-named-target NL relation only through an internal exit-then-guarded-reentry pattern (state -> [*] with effect setting R45RouteToken, then a guarded outer transition testing R45RouteToken). This satisfies reachability of the target from the source in the finite graph sense (verify_facts marks these reachable and event-consumer proved), so I treat those as satisfied for behavior-consequence purposes and do not re-litigate S2 endpoint identity here (that is the structural-contrast lens's job). My distinct contribution is on termination stability, guard-disjointness-as-behavior, and effect-consequence for state retention/timer semantics, plus unresolved rows for entry/do-activity obligations whose exact carrier does not exist in the closed model's parsed schema.

decisions.basis: NL5 requirement quote 'where the cooking time is displayed and updated'; fcstm_model.text lines 20-27,39-44; inspection_equivalent_facts state records for ReadytoCook/WaitingToStart.
decisions.reason: NL5 explicitly requires a display/update-cooking-time action. decisions.violated_obligation: NL5 requires an entry action on ReadytoCook (or WaitingToStart) that displays and updates the cooking-time value.

decisions.basis: NL6 requirement quote 'canceling or updating the cooking time'; fcstm_model.text lines 28,33,40; inspection_equivalent_facts transition effect records.

decisions.violated_obligation: NL6 requires the Cancel-triggered ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem transition to carry an effect cancelling/updating the cooking-time value.

One state-action obligation (i2) had an executed S4 predicate returning verdict=false, establishing the entry-action absence, though a weak undercutting alternative about global timing abstraction survives. Several action/effect obligations (i0, i1, i3, i4) had no executable predicate but exact model facts (only R45RouteToken generic route-control effects, no domain-specific timer/cooking-time variables) established the absence of the required domain content, with a competent but unconfirmed undercutting alternative reading surviving (that R45RouteToken abstractly stands in for the missing domain effect). i7 was rebutted: a PlantUML description line is not executable semantics, and the closed model's consistency with declaration semantics is a positive rebuttal. i6 and i8 were left unresolved because the supplied dossier lacks executed SMT/backend resolution (i6) or lacks any resolved element/owner identity (i8), and the exact facts genuinely cannot decide the property.

decisions.basis: fcstm_model.text lines 20-27, 39-44; inspection_equivalent_facts for states ReadytoCook/WaitingToStart; NL5 contract text; binding over ModelIR state:ReadytoCook:line:20 and state:WaitingToStart:line:28.
decisions.reason: NL5's requirement_quote 'where the cooking time is displayed and updated' expects a dedicated cooking-time display/update action attached to ReadytoCook or WaitingToStart. The exact closed-model facts (fcstm_model.text lines 20-27, 39-44) show ReadytoCook and WaitingToStart carry no entry/exit action, and the only recorded effects on incoming transitions are R45RouteToken assignments, a generic route-control integer unrelated to cooking-time semantics. The candidate itself raises and rejects the alternative that R45RouteToken could stand in for the cooking-time variable, but the model text nowhere ties R45RouteToken to a display/update of a cooking-time domain value, so this rebuttal is defeated by the exact closed inventory. No undercutting alternative scope/member reading survives because ReadytoCook/WaitingToStart are precisely and uniquely bound as the loci for this NL5 obligation.
decisions.strongest_defeater: If R45RouteToken or an unlisted variable were interpreted as the cooking-time value, the assignment could arguably represent an update, but the model text and inspection facts show only a generic route-control integer, not a cooking-time variable or display side-effect.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL5 requires an entry action on ReadytoCook (or its owned WaitingToStart substate) that displays and updates the cooking-time value.

decisions.basis: fcstm_model.text lines 28, 33, 40; inspection_equivalent_facts transitions line:33 and line:40; NL6 contract text; binding over ModelIR transition:line:33 and transition:line:40.
decisions.reason: NL6's requirement_quote 'canceling or updating the cooking time' calls for an effect on the routed ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem transition that manipulates a cooking-time value. The exact bound transitions (line 33: WaitingToStart->[*] effect R45RouteToken=13; line 40: ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem guard R45RouteToken==13 effect R45RouteToken=0) only manipulate the generic route-control variable R45RouteToken, with no cooking-time-specific field anywhere in the closed FCSTM. The candidate's own rebuttal, that resetting the route token to 0 is an abstract cancel signal, is defeated because the model provides no linkage between R45RouteToken and any cooking-time semantics; it is a pure routing artifact. No undercutting alternative member reading survives since the transition pair carrying this Cancel-triggered behavior is exactly and uniquely bound.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The route-token reset to 0 could be read as an abstract 'cancel' of pending state, but it is not tied to any cooking-time variable in the model, so it does not satisfy a domain cooking-time cancel/update obligation.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL6 requires that the Cancel-triggered ReadytoCook-to-DoorShutWithItem transition carry an effect canceling or updating the cooking-time value.

The FCSTM state label text 'DoorShut\n[PlantUML body] Cancel' embeds 'Cancel' only as an inert body/action-note artifact, not a modeled transition or trigger. event_consumers shows no Cancel consumer state is DoorShut (Cancel's reachable consumers are only WaitingToStart and ActiveCooking).
issues.reason: NL1 explicitly requires that performing Cancel while in DoorShut leaves the system in DoorShut, i.e., an observable retained-state behavior in response to the Cancel event. The closed model has zero transitions tied to Cancel at DoorShut; the only trace of 'Cancel' is inert body text carried into the FCSTM state name, which is not an executable retention mechanism.
issues.requirement_quote: the system can either remain in DoorShut if a Cancel action is performed
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML source shows 'DoorShut : Cancel' as an internal state action/note rather than a self-transition, so the NL retention obligation may be intended as a benign no-op action rather than a modeled transition; however the NL explicitly frames Cancel as one of two alternative behavioral outcomes ('either remain ... or transition'), which requires an observable state-retention semantics, not merely a textual annotation.
issues.title: DoorShut has no self-loop or any transition triggered by Cancel

issues.basis: smt_facts.formulas entries for transition:line:47/48 equivalent effects (R45RouteToken=6/10/11 etc.), solver_status=not_run across all 14 formulas; inspection_equivalent_facts transitions at line 47 (Close_Door_with_Zero_Time) and line 48 (Enter_Cooking_Time) with disjoint triggers; NL-CONTRACT-NL4-DISJOINT-1 normative statement.
issues.expected: The two alternative continuations from the DoorOpenWithItem-scoped exit (zero-time-close vs cooking-time-entered) must be mutually exclusive/distinguishable so exactly one alternative fires for a given stimulus.
issues.observed: In the closed FCSTM, the two named events (Close_Door_with_Zero_Time at transition:line:47, Enter_Cooking_Time at transition:line:48) are distinct triggers from DoorIdleWithItem, which is event-level disjoint at that carrier. However, the actually observable behavioral outcome of the whole DoorOpenWithItem-scoped alternative (reaching DoorShutWithItem vs ReadytoCook) is realized through the shared R45RouteToken exit/guard mechanism (transitions:line:52-55 test disjoint integer literals 10/14/17 and guard:transition:line:38/39 test 10/11), whose guards are simple disjoint integer equalities with solver_status='not_run' for all relevant formulas, so no deterministic proof of exclusivity is available at the SMT layer for the composite behavioral relation.
issues.reason: The obligation compares two alternatives sharing one behavioral relation; because their guard-fact backing is delegated through unresolved SMT formulas (solver_status=not_run) and the direct NL-level trigger pairing is realized via an unrelated internal composite-exit encoding rather than a directly guarded pair at one shared carrier, the precise distinguishability claim cannot be certified by any frozen predicate and remains a precise but unresolved semantic property.
issues.requirement_quote: the system can transition to DoorShutWithItem if the door is closed with zero time set or to ReadytoCook if cooking time is entered
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Each individual route-token guard is a literal equality on the same variable with distinct integer constants (6,10,11,13,14,17,18,19), which are trivially mutually exclusive by construction; the disjointness may already be evident from guard syntax without needing SMT solving, undermining the need for a violation candidate here.
issues.title: DoorOpenWithItem alternatives are event-keyed, not condition-keyed; disjointness rests on unresolved SMT guards downstream

decisions.reason: NL5's requirement_quote 'where the cooking time is displayed and updated' expects a dedicated cooking-time display/update action attached to ReadytoCook or WaitingToStart. The exact closed-model facts (fcstm_model.text lines 20-27, 39-44) show ReadytoCook and WaitingToStart carry no entry/exit action, and the only recorded effects on incoming transitions are R45RouteToken assignments, a generic route-control integer unrelated to cooking-time semantics. The candidate itself raises and rejects the alternative that R45RouteToken could stand in for the cooking-time variable, but the model text nowhere ties R45RouteToken to a display/update of a cooking-time domain value, so this rebuttal is defeated by the exact closed inventory. No undercutting alternative scope/member reading survives because ReadytoCook/WaitingToStart are precisely and uniquely bound as the loci for this NL5 obligation.
decisions.strongest_defeater: If R45RouteToken or an unlisted variable were interpreted as the cooking-time value, the assignment could arguably represent an update, but the model text and inspection facts show only a generic route-control integer, not a cooking-time variable or display side-effect.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL5 requires an entry action on ReadytoCook (or its owned WaitingToStart substate) that displays and updates the cooking-time value.

decisions.basis: fcstm_model.text lines 28, 33, 40; inspection_equivalent_facts transitions line:33 and line:40; NL6 contract text; binding over ModelIR transition:line:33 and transition:line:40.
decisions.reason: NL6's requirement_quote 'canceling or updating the cooking time' calls for an effect on the routed ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem transition that manipulates a cooking-time value. The exact bound transitions (line 33: WaitingToStart->[*] effect R45RouteToken=13; line 40: ReadytoCook->DoorShutWithItem guard R45RouteToken==13 effect R45RouteToken=0) only manipulate the generic route-control variable R45RouteToken, with no cooking-time-specific field anywhere in the closed FCSTM. The candidate's own rebuttal, that resetting the route token to 0 is an abstract cancel signal, is defeated because the model provides no linkage between R45RouteToken and any cooking-time semantics; it is a pure routing artifact. No undercutting alternative member reading survives since the transition pair carrying this Cancel-triggered behavior is exactly and uniquely bound.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The route-token reset to 0 could be read as an abstract 'cancel' of pending state, but it is not tied to any cooking-time variable in the model, so it does not satisfy a domain cooking-time cancel/update obligation.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL6 requires that the Cancel-triggered ReadytoCook-to-DoorShutWithItem transition carry an effect canceling or updating the cooking-time value.

Most NL transition endpoints are satisfied through the compiler's macro-generated route-token relay pattern (each authored source-target edge is realized via a routed pair: an outgoing segment setting R45RouteToken to a code, an ascend-to-owner completion transition consuming that code with matching guard, and a re-entry/decision at the owning scope). Root-level DoorShut/DoorOpen endpoints are direct. The DoorOpenWithItem group's alternatives are fully guard-disjoint (each token code is unique: 6/10/14/17/18/19 etc.), so the guard_disjointness contract is satisfied for the routed set. The NL4 alternatives specifically route through distinct completion codes (10 and then 11) which are disjoint. The two action/effect contracts (NL5-ACTION, NL7-ACTION, NL8-STATEACTION, NL6-EFFECT, NL8-EFFECT, NL1-DERIVED trigger, NL5-DERIVED effect) require action/effect content that pyfcstm's parsed guard/effect model expresses only as the R45RouteToken assignment, not as domain actions like 'display cooking time' or 'start timer' or 'stop timer' -- these remain unsupported semantic gaps (W1, predicate null) since no state entry/exit action or transition effect carries the domain-specific content; only the generic route variable is set. I flag these as candidates since the exact carrier transitions/states exist but lack the required domain content.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, stable termination, cross-wrapper reachability, and dead-end frontier facts, using the closed FCSTM inspection-equivalent, verify, and SMT facts against the NL contracts. Key finding: the microwave PlantUML has a top-level DoorShut/DoorOpen/DoorOpenWithItem layer while the FCSTM instead nests all DoorOpenWithItem-scope activity under a compiler-owned wrapper reached through internal pseudo-exit routing (R45RouteToken) rather than direct named-state transitions. All NL-named states are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection-equivalent facts, and all declared events have reachable consumers per event_consumers facts, so root reachability and event-consumer coverage contracts are broadly satisfied at the structural level. However, several transition_endpoints contracts require inspection of the exact carrier because the closed FCSTM realizes each named-source-to-named-target NL relation only through an internal exit-then-guarded-reentry pattern (state -> [*] with effect setting R45RouteToken, then a guarded outer transition testing R45RouteToken). This satisfies reachability of the target from the source in the finite graph sense (verify_facts marks these reachable and event-consumer proved), so I treat those as satisfied for behavior-consequence purposes and do not re-litigate S2 endpoint identity here (that is the structural-contrast lens's job). My distinct contribution is on termination stability, guard-disjointness-as-behavior, and effect-consequence for state retention/timer semantics, plus unresolved rows for entry/do-activity obligations whose exact carrier does not exist in the closed model's parsed schema.
